subject.title: [Feature]: Pluggable STT backend for macOS Push-to-Talk

question: Should native macOS Push-to-Talk get a batch STT backend seam now, and should that seam bridge to existing Gateway `tools.media.audio`/provider contracts or be folded into the broader native custom-ASR design?
rationale: This changes native app behavior, provider/auth routing, private-network exposure, fallback policy, and possibly config/UI surface, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product/security boundary.

options.title: Design the PTT batch seam first
options.body: Keep Apple Speech as the default, add a final-text batch backend for PTT, and reuse existing Gateway media-audio/provider security contracts for configured STT backends.

options.title: Fold into the custom-ASR parent
options.body: Move the PTT-specific requirements into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46661 and close or narrow this issue once the parent owns the complete native ASR scope.

options.title: Defer native STT backend selection
options.body: Leave native PTT on Apple Speech until maintainers are ready to own the endpoint/auth/private-network and overlay UX design.

recommendation.title: Design the PTT batch seam first
recommendation.body: Keep Apple Speech as the default, add a final-text batch backend for PTT, and reuse existing Gateway media-audio/provider security contracts for configured STT backends.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` has the strongest native macOS voice/PTT history in the affected Swift files and is the best available owner for the product boundary choice.
